Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

[MATH: \left| s - \dfrac{7}{6} \right| - 11 = -5]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we isolate the absolute value by adding [MATH: 11] to both sides:

[MATH: |s − (7)/(6)|− 11|= − 5;|s − (7)/(6)||= 6]

Next, we consider both possible cases for the absolute value.

  • If [MATH: \left| s - \dfrac{7}{6} \right| = s - \dfrac{7}{6},] then [MATH: |s − (7)/(6)||= 6; s − (7)/(6)|= 6; s|= (7)/(6) + 6; s|= (7)/(6) + (36)/(6); s|= (43)/(6).]

  • If [MATH: \left| s - \dfrac{7}{6} \right| = -\!\left( s - \dfrac{7}{6} \right),] then [MATH: |s − (7)/(6)||= 6; − (s − (7)/(6))|= 6; − s + (7)/(6)|= 6; − s|= 6 − (7)/(6); − s|= (36)/(6) − (7)/(6); − s|= (29)/(6); s|= − (29)/(6).]

Therefore, the sum of the solutions is [MATH: \dfrac{43}{6} + \left(-\dfrac{29}{6}\right) = \dfrac{14}{6} = \dfrac{7}{3}.]

items.readable_text:
Example Prompt:
What is the sum of the solutions to the equation given below?
[MATH: \left| \dfrac{3}{5}x - \dfrac{11}{6} \right| = \dfrac{7}{3}]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To solve this equation, we consider both possible cases for the absolute value.

- If [MATH: \left|\dfrac{3}{5}x - \dfrac{11}{6}\right| = \dfrac{3}{5}x - \dfrac{11}{6},] then
[MATH: |(3)/(5)x − (11)/(6)||= (7)/(3); (3)/(5)x − (11)/(6)|= (7)/(3); (3)/(5)x|= (7)/(3) + (11)/(6); (3)/(5)x|= (14)/(6) + (11)/(6); (3)/(5)x|= (25)/(6); x|= (25)/(6) ⋅ (5)/(3); x|= (125)/(18).]
- If [MATH: \left|\dfrac{3}{5}x - \dfrac{11}{6}\right| = -\left(\dfrac{3}{5}x - \dfrac{11}{6}\right),] then
[MATH: |(3)/(5)x − (11)/(6)||= (7)/(3); − ((3)/(5)x − (11)/(6))|= (7)/(3); − (3)/(5)x + (11)/(6)|= (7)/(3); − (3)/(5)x|= (7)/(3) − (11)/(6); − (3)/(5)x|= (14)/(6) − (11)/(6); − (3)/(5)x|= (3)/(6); x|= (3)/(6) ⋅ (− (5)/(3)); x|= − (15)/(18); x|= − (5)/(6).]

Therefore, the sum of the solutions is
[MATH: \dfrac{125}{18} + \left(-\dfrac{5}{6}\right) = \dfrac{125}{18} - \dfrac{15}{18} = \dfrac{110}{18} = \dfrac{55}{9}.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In this topic, we'll practice solving absolute value equations. In some cases, we need to first collect like terms that contain absolute value expressions before solving.

---

Item 2 — Example: Solving One-Step Absolute Value Equations

Example Prompt:
Which of the following is a possible solution to the equation [MATH: |-x - 6| = 5?]

1. [MATH: x = 1]
2. [MATH: x = -11]
3. [MATH: x = -6]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To solve the equation [MATH: |-x - 6| = 5,] we consider both possible cases for the absolute value.

- If [MATH: |-x - 6| = -x - 6,] then
[MATH: |− x − 6||= 5; − x − 6|= 5; − x|= 11; x|= − 11.]
- If [MATH: |-x - 6| = -(-x - 6),] then
[MATH: |− x − 6||= 5; − (− x − 6)|= 5; x + 6|= 5; x|= − 1.]

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

Item 5 — Example: Solving an Equation by Isolating an Absolute Value Expression

Content:

Explanation:
First, we isolate the absolute value by adding [MATH: 11] to both sides:

[MATH: |s − (7)/(6)|− 11|= − 5;|s − (7)/(6)||= 6]

Next, we consider both possible cases for the absolute value.

- If [MATH: \left| s - \dfrac{7}{6} \right| = s - \dfrac{7}{6},] then
[MATH: |s − (7)/(6)||= 6; s − (7)/(6)|= 6; s|= (7)/(6) + 6; s|= (7)/(6) + (36)/(6); s|= (43)/(6).]
- If [MATH: \left| s - \dfrac{7}{6} \right| = -\!\left( s - \dfrac{7}{6} \right),] then
[MATH: |s − (7)/(6)||= 6; − (s − (7)/(6))|= 6; − s + (7)/(6)|= 6; − s|= 6 − (7)/(6); − s|= (36)/(6) − (7)/(6); − s|= (29)/(6); s|= − (29)/(6).]

[MATH: \dfrac{43}{6} + \left(-\dfrac{29}{6}\right) = \dfrac{14}{6} = \dfrac{7}{3}.]

[MATH: \left| \dfrac{3}{5}x - \dfrac{11}{6} \right| = \dfrac{7}{3}]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To solve this equation, we consider both possible cases for the absolute value.

- If [MATH: \left|\dfrac{3}{5}x - \dfrac{11}{6}\right| = \dfrac{3}{5}x - \dfrac{11}{6},] then
[MATH: |(3)/(5)x − (11)/(6)||= (7)/(3); (3)/(5)x − (11)/(6)|= (7)/(3); (3)/(5)x|= (7)/(3) + (11)/(6); (3)/(5)x|= (14)/(6) + (11)/(6); (3)/(5)x|= (25)/(6); x|= (25)/(6) ⋅ (5)/(3); x|= (125)/(18).]

Therefore, the sum of the solutions is
[MATH: \dfrac{125}{18} + \left(-\dfrac{5}{6}\right) = \dfrac{125}{18} - \dfrac{15}{18} = \dfrac{110}{18} = \dfrac{55}{9}.]
